The seasonal announcements on the front page carry three more dated prices, recorded below as seasonal. Everything else has an empty price rather than an invented one. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE FINDING HERE IS A VEGAN RAMEN ON A 1954-STYLE ASAKUSA COUNTER, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST ILLUSTRATION IN THIS DATASET OF THE TWO DIETS COMING APART. ヴィーガンらーめん at ¥1,400 is a real, permanent, priced menu item at a traditional 和風醤油 ramen shop on Denboin-dori — which is worth knowing, because a vegan in Asakusa otherwise has very little. But a vegan ramen is not a gluten-free ramen and nothing about it moves the coeliac answer: the noodles are wheat with かん水 whatever the broth is made of, and the tare on a 醤油 bowl is soy. One diet gets a whole dish; the other gets nothing, from the same bowl. ⚠ ONE BOWL IS WORTH ASKING ABOUT ON THE OTHER AXIS: 梅しおらーめん and the しお option on the 特製 use a SALT tare rather than a soy one, which removes one of the two wheat routes. The noodle is the other and it remains, so this is a distinction that matters for understanding the kitchen rather than one that opens the door. ⚠ AND THE SEASONAL BOWLS ADD RATHER THAN SUBTRACT: the 冷やし中華 comes 特製ごまだれ付き — a sesame dressing, which in Japan is built on soy — and the 坦々つけ麺 is a sesame-and-soy dip. 伝法院通り, Asakusa.

It is recorded as partial for that reason, not because the numbers are shaky: the site publishes the Kabukicho board in Japanese and English on two separate pages and the two agree item-for-item and yen-for-yen, which is the strongest cross-check available for a shop of this kind. Address 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町2-37-5, 11:30-02:30, closed Wednesdays (the site adds 営業する日も有り — it sometimes opens anyway). ⚠ THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE RESEARCH, IT IS THE DISH. Jiro is a wheat-noodle form: the noodles are thick 極太 wheat with かん水, the tare is soy, and the broth is pork back-fat and bone. Every bowl on the board is wheat by construction and there is no rice, no side and no non-noodle item to fall back on — the entire menu is eight noodle bowls and four toppings. ⚠ AND THE FREE CALL SYSTEM DOES NOT HELP EITHER, WHICH IS THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING. Jiro's famous no-charge コール at the counter — ニンニク／ヤサイ／アブラ／カラメ, garlic, vegetables, back-fat, extra tare — reads like a way to customise around an ingredient, and it is not: ヤサイ is boiled beansprouts and cabbage piled on the same wheat noodles in the same bowl, and カラメ means MORE of the soy tare, i.e. more wheat. The calls change the mountain, never the base. ⚠ ONE VEGAN-ADJACENT TRAP ON THE TOPPING LIST: 生とじ卵 is a raw egg served with 魚粉, bonito powder — a fish product sitting in what looks like a plain egg topping.

tokyo_canaru_shinjuku_restaura.price_note: CANARD publishes its dinner card on its own site (menu.html, a Shift-JIS page off the shop's long-running 2009 template). ⚠ READ THESE PRICES AS A COURSE, NOT A LIST. Dinner is 4,500円 before tax for カナルディナー — one hors d'oeuvre, one main and one cheese-or-dessert chosen from the lists below — or 7,500円 before tax for the chef's おまかせグルメディナー of hors d'oeuvre, fish, palate cleanser, meat and dessert. The ＋xxx円 figures recorded against individual dishes are SUPPLEMENTS ADDED TO THE COURSE PRICE, not standalone prices, and a dish carrying no figure carries no supplement. The shop's own footer says the in-store menu takes precedence and that every price shown is before tax. Service 18:00–22:30 (last order); parties from 15 people, tel 03-3200-0706. ⚠ FRENCH BISTRO COOKING IS FLOUR-FIRST AND ALMOST NOTHING ON THIS CARD IS SAFE TO ASSUME. Poêlé fish is dusted in flour as a matter of technique, cream and wine sauces are classically roux-thickened, and a fricassée IS a flour-bound stew. Three dishes are wheat by name rather than by inference — the キッシュ and the スズキのパイ包み焼き are pastry, and the オニオングラタンスープ is gratinéed over a slice of bread — and the two tarts are pastry as well. Everything else is an ask, which at a small owner-run French room is a conversation worth having rather than a dead end. ⚠ AND THERE IS NO VEGAN ROUTE THROUGH THIS CARD AT ALL: every hors d'oeuvre is fish, meat, egg or cheese, every main is an animal, and the desserts are dairy — a plant-only diner cannot assemble a course here, and the closest thing to a vegetable starter, the ズッキーニ, is sauced in Roquefort.

tokyo_sushi_shabu_shabu_yuzuan.price_note: ゆず庵 (物語コーポレーション) publishes its whole board with BOTH the pre-tax and tax-included figure on every line; both are recorded below exactly as printed. Branch confirmed: ゆず庵 新宿西口大ガード店, 東京都新宿区西新宿7-1-1 新宿カレイドビル6F, 10:30–24:00, with wheelchair-accessible seating. The chain's own footnotes qualify all of it: 「商品の一部を記載しています」, 「仕入れ状況により内容を変更する場合がございます」 and 「店舗により商品内容および価格が異なる場合がございます」 — so this is most of the board at chain prices, not a guarantee for this branch. ⚠ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THE ENTIRE MENU IS A FOOTNOTE UNDER THE NOODLES AND IT IS PRINTED TWICE: 「※当店の麺類はそばと同じ釜で茹でています」 — EVERY NOODLE IN THE SHOP IS BOILED IN THE SAME POT AS THE SOBA. That is a shared-water declaration made voluntarily by the operator, and it means the udon, the ramen noodle, the harusame and the two udon 〆 dishes all carry buckwheat contact whether or not they contain buckwheat. For a coeliac it is moot — udon and chuka men are wheat anyway — but for a buckwheat allergy, which in Japan is the more dangerous of the two, it rules out the entire noodle section including the ones that look safe. ⚠ THE CHAIN PUBLISHES A REAL ALLERGEN TABLE AND YOU CANNOT READ IT ON A SCREEN. monogatari.co.jp/allergy/brand/yuzu.php offers a 26-category allergen chart covering Japan's eight 特定原材料 — えび・かに・くるみ・小麦・そば・卵・乳・落花生 (shrimp, crab, walnut, WHEAT, BUCKWHEAT, egg, milk, peanut), last updated 2026-08-25 — but it is served only as an image-scan PDF whose text layer is empty, so it cannot be transcribed here. It IS worth opening in the shop. Note what that eight-item list does NOT include: barley and rye are outside Japan's statutory scheme entirely, so 麦味噌 and beer will never be flagged by it. ⚠ AND THE OPERATOR'S OWN CONTAMINATION NOTICE IS UNUSUALLY BLUNT, WHICH MATTERS MORE HERE THAN AT MOST RESTAURANTS: 「店舗では、アレルギー物質を含む原材料と共通の設備・調理器具で調理・盛付し、共通の食器を使用しております」 — shared equipment, shared utensils, shared tableware. THIS IS A DIY HOTPOT RESTAURANT: the guest cooks their own meat and vegetables in a shared pot at the table, so gluten from a wheat noodle, a dumpling or a tteok goes into the same broth everyone is eating from. There is no way to run a strict coeliac protocol at a shabu-shabu table where somebody else is cooking udon in it. ⚠ THE 2色鍋だし CHOICE AT 580円 IS THE ONE PLACE A REAL DECISION GETS MADE, AND FOUR OF THE FIVE BROTHS ARE OUT: すき焼きだし is soy and mirin, 牛骨旨辛 麻辣湯だし is beef bone, 鰹一番だし is bonito, and 塩レモンだし is undescribed. ゆず庵昆布だし — kombu — IS THE ONLY ONE THAT READS AS PLANT-BASED AND WHEAT-FREE ON ITS NAME, and it is the single most useful thing to know before sitting down. Two broths are chosen per pot, so a vegan would need both halves to be the kombu one, which the menu does not say is possible. ⚠ ONE MORE OPERATOR FOOTNOTE WORTH CARRYING: 「※鶏しゃぶしゃぶは形を整える加工をしています」 — the chicken shabu is a FORMED product, not a sliced cut, which is exactly the sort of item that carries binder. And an egg surcharge is in force: 「卵の価格高騰の影響により、追加の卵は別途50円（税込55円）」.

The broths on the sets are fixed as ゆず庵昆布だし and すき焼きだし, and the sukiyaki half is soy — so the set removes the one choice that mattered. Tempura and chawanmushi make it wheat regardless.

tokyo_bangkok_spice_shinjuku.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own site (新宿区西新宿1-14-4 小黒ビル1F — behind Yodobashi, matching the record's Nishi-Shinjuku placement). Heat is marked ☆ to ☆☆☆☆ on the shop's own card and those marks are reproduced below. ⚠ THE HEADLINE FINDING IS THE 麺 SECTION, WHERE RICE AND WHEAT NOODLES SIT SIDE BY SIDE UNLABELLED. The shop states 米粉 (rice flour) outright for its トムヤムクンヌードル, and クイッティオ is a rice noodle by definition — three of them here. But two dishes in the same block are wheat and nothing on the card says so: カオソーイ is northern-Thai khao soi, which is made with WHEAT EGG NOODLES rather than rice, and グリーンカレーうどん is udon, i.e. wheat, hiding at the bottom of the CURRY section rather than the noodle one. パッシーユー is 'pad see ew', which is named for see ew — SOY SAUCE — so its wide rice noodle arrives in wheat seasoning, and パッキーマオ is the same wide noodle in the same style. ⚠ 海老トースト is bread and 揚げ春巻き uses a wheat wrapper; the 生春巻き is rice paper and is the better bet. Thai fish sauce, oyster sauce and curry pastes are the recurring 'ask' — most contain shrimp paste and fish sauce, so the curries are not vegan, and Japanese-market oyster and seasoning sauces frequently carry wheat. ⚠ VEGAN: the shop makes no vegan claim and there is no meat-free curry or stir-fry on the card; ヤムメッマモアン (cashew salad) and the plain rice lines are the only unambiguous plant items, and ソムタム and the salads are dressed with fish sauce as standard.

items.en: Southern-Thai dry curry of minced pork, ☆☆☆☆ — the shop calls it numbing heat
items.note: A southern curry paste built on shrimp paste and fish sauce; wheat is not inherent but Japanese-market seasoning sauces often carry it. Ask.

items.ja: ピークガイトード(鶏手羽揚げガーリックorトムヤム味)
items.en: Fried chicken wings, garlic or tom yum flavour
items.note: Thai fried wings are dredged in a wheat-and-rice flour mix and share the fryer with the spring rolls and prawn toast.

items.ja: ラープ(タイ風コロッケ)
items.en: The shop's larb served as a Thai-style croquette
items.note: The shop describes this one as a コロッケ — a croquette, so breadcrumbed and fried. Note it is a different dish from the ラープガイ salad further down the card, which is not fried.

items.ja: クントーソースマカーム(揚げ海老のタマリンドソース)
items.en: Fried prawns in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce
items.note: Battered and fried; tamarind sauces in a Japanese kitchen are commonly cut with soy or oyster sauce.

items.ja: シーフードガパオ(色々シーフードのガパオ炒め)
items.en: Mixed seafood stir-fried with holy basil, ☆☆☆
items.note: Gapao is seasoned with fish sauce and oyster sauce; Japanese-market oyster sauce routinely contains wheat. Ask.

items.ja: ヤムパクチー(パクチーサラダ)
items.note: Thai yam dressings are lime, chilli and FISH SAUCE — not vegan, and the fish sauce brand's wheat status is unpublished.

items.ja: プラーラプリック(揚げ魚の甘辛いソースかけ)
items.en: Fried fish under a sweet chilli sauce
items.note: The fish is floured before frying and the sauce is a thickened sweet-chilli.

items.ja: クイッティオガパオ(ガパオ麺)
items.note: クイッティオ is a RICE noodle — the noodle itself is clear. The gapao seasoning (fish sauce, oyster sauce) is the open question.

items.ja: ラープガイ（鶏ひき肉のスパイシーサラダ）
items.note: Larb is dressed with lime, roasted rice powder, chilli and fish sauce — the roasted rice is rice, not wheat. Fish sauce composition unpublished.

items.ja: ナムトックムー（豚肉とハーブのスパイシーサラダ）
items.note: Same dressing family as larb — fish sauce and lime.

items.ja: プラーク（海老のレモングラスサラダ）
items.note: Fish-sauce dressing.

items.ja: ラーププラーマグロ (生マグロのユッケ)
items.note: The shop calls it a yukhoe, which in Japan usually means a soy-and-sesame dressing; the Thai reading would be fish sauce. Ask which.

items.ja: ムーマナーオ(豚肉の激辛レモンソースかけ)
items.en: Poached pork in a fiery lime sauce, ☆☆☆
items.note: Lime, garlic, chilli and fish sauce.

items.ja: ヤムメッマモアン(カシューナッツのタイ風サラダ)
items.note: The only salad on the card whose named ingredient is not animal — but the standard Thai dressing still carries fish sauce, and the cashews are often fried. Ask; this is the dish to ask about if you are avoiding meat.

items.ja: パクチーサラダ(シーフードとひき肉とパクチーのタイ風ドレッシング合え)
items.en: Coriander salad with seafood and minced meat in Thai dressing, ☆☆
items.note: Fish-sauce dressing.

items.ja: ポーピーアソッド(生春巻き)
items.note: Fresh rolls use RICE paper, unlike the fried version on this card — a real distinction and the better bet. But the dipping sauce is unpublished and Thai fresh rolls normally carry prawn or pork.

items.ja: ヤムウンセン（春雨サラダ）
items.note: ウンセン glass noodles are mung-bean starch, not wheat. The dressing is fish sauce and the salad normally carries minced pork and prawn.

items.ja: ソムタムタイ（青パパイヤのサラダ）
items.note: Som tam is pounded with dried shrimp and fish sauce as standard.

items.ja: ソムタムプーパラ
items.en: Green papaya salad with pickled crab and fermented fish
items.note: Pla ra is fermented fish — strongly not vegan, and its production sometimes uses rice bran or other cereals.

items.ja: ヤムタレー(シーフードサラダ)
items.note: Fish-sauce dressing.

items.ja: ミアンムータカイ（豚挽き肉と色々ハーブの）
items.en: Minced pork and mixed herb wraps, ☆☆☆
items.note: Miang is wrapped in leaf rather than pastry; the sauce is fish-sauce based.

items.ja: ラープヘッド（タイ風キノコサラダ）
items.note: Mushroom rather than meat — the closest thing to a vegetarian main-sized dish on the card. Larb dressing is still fish sauce as standard, so ask whether it can be made without.

items.ja: ヤムパックプントース(揚げ空芯菜のスパイシーサラダ)
items.en: Crispy fried water spinach in a spicy salad, ☆☆
items.note: The greens are battered and deep-fried — Thai crispy-vegetable batter is a wheat-and-rice flour mix, in the shared fryer. Dressing is fish sauce.

items.ja: ガイヤーン（鶏肉のグリル）
items.note: Gai yang marinade is fish sauce, garlic, coriander root and often oyster sauce. Ask about the oyster sauce specifically.

items.ja: コウムーヤーン（豚トロのグリル）
items.note: Marinated in a soy-or-oyster-sauce mixture as standard, and served with a fiery dipping sauce. Ask.

items.ja: クンパオ 2尾（大海老のグリル）
items.note: Plain grilled prawn is the cleanest protein on this card; the seafood dipping sauce beside it is lime, chilli, garlic and fish sauce. Ask.

items.ja: カイジョウムゥ（タイ風豚肉の卵焼き）
items.note: Egg and pork, seasoned with fish sauce; deep-fried in the shared oil.

items.ja: サテ(2本)ガイ（鶏肉のタイ風串焼きピーナツソース添え）
items.en: Two chicken satay skewers with peanut sauce
items.note: Satay peanut sauce commonly contains fish sauce or shrimp paste and sometimes soy. Ask.

items.ja: プーンムプリックァー（ソフトシェルのピリ辛揚げ）

items.ja: ガイタカイ（鶏肉とレモングラス揚げ）
items.note: Dredged and fried in the shared oil.

items.ja: カノムパンナークン（海老トースト）
items.note: Wheat bread, deep-fried.

items.ja: ポーピアトーサワン(揚げ生春巻き)／ポーピアクントース(海老春巻き)／ポーピアトース(揚げ春巻き)
items.note: Thai fried spring-roll wrappers are wheat, unlike the fresh rice-paper rolls listed among the starters.

items.ja: トーマンクン（魚のさつま揚げ）
items.note: Tod man is bound and crumbed with wheat as standard.

items.ja: エンガイトース(鶏なんこつ揚げ)
items.note: Dredged and fried.

items.ja: プーニムパッポンカリー（ソフトシェルと卵のカレー炒め）
items.en: Soft-shell crab stir-fried in yellow curry with egg, ☆
items.note: The crab is battered and fried first; the sauce carries evaporated milk and oyster sauce as standard.

items.ja: パッチャウゴウ（シーフードの激辛トムヤムソース炒め）
items.en: Seafood stir-fried in a fiery tom yum sauce, ☆☆☆☆
items.note: Fish sauce and chilli paste; Thai chilli pastes usually contain shrimp paste.

items.ja: パッガパオ（鶏肉／豚肉のガパオ炒め）
items.note: Fish sauce plus oyster sauce; Japanese-market oyster sauce routinely contains wheat. This is the single most-asked-about dish on any Thai card — ask specifically about the oyster sauce.

items.ja: パッガパオクランナイガイ(鶏砂肝のガパオ)
items.note: As above.

items.ja: ガイパッメットマムアン (鶏肉とカシューナッツ炒め)
items.note: This dish is built on oyster sauce and soy sauce and the chicken is normally floured before frying.

items.ja: パッパックプンファイデーン (空芯菜炒め)
items.note: Vegetable-only in the pan, which makes it the most plant-forward hot dish here — but the standard seasoning is fermented bean curd, oyster sauce and fish sauce. Ask what it is seasoned with.

items.ja: トウミョウファイデーン (豆苗炒め)
items.note: As above — vegetable-only in the pan, seasoning unpublished. The cheapest plant dish on the card.

items.ja: コマツナムゥコウ (カリカリ豚と小松菜のオイスターソース炒め)
items.en: Crispy pork and komatsuna in oyster sauce, ☆☆
items.note: The card names OYSTER SAUCE outright, which in Japan routinely contains wheat, and the pork is crisped in flour.

items.ja: ホイマレンプーオップ（ムール貝の土鍋蒸し）
items.en: Mussels steamed in a clay pot
items.note: Steamed with lemongrass and herbs; the dipping sauce is fish-sauce based.

items.ja: クンオップクァー(蒸し海老のタイソース)
items.note: Thai steamed-prawn sauces are usually soy-and-oyster based. Ask.

items.ja: カイヌン(蒸し鶏のにんにく生姜ソース)
items.en: Steamed chicken with garlic and ginger sauce
items.note: Steamed rather than fried, so the coating question does not arise — the sauce does. Ask.

items.ja: トムヤムクン（海老とレモングラスの酸味の利いた辛いスープ）
items.en: Tom yum kung, ☆☆ — the shop calls it one of the world's three great soups
items.note: Prawn stock, fish sauce and nam prik pao chilli paste; the chilli paste normally contains shrimp paste.

items.ja: トムカーガイ(鶏肉のスパイスと酸味の効いたココナッツミルク味スープ)
items.note: Coconut, galangal, lime and fish sauce.

items.ja: ゲーンジュー(あっさり野菜スープ)
items.note: The card's lightest dish and the one most worth asking about for a plant eater — but gaeng jued is conventionally a pork-bone stock with minced pork, and the shop does not say otherwise.

items.ja: ゲーンオムウンセン(鶏肉の激辛春雨スープ)
items.note: Glass noodles are mung-bean starch, not wheat; the curry paste and fish sauce are the question.

items.ja: ゲーンキョウワーン（グリーンカレー）鶏肉／豚肉
items.en: Green curry, chicken or pork — meat is your choice, ☆☆
items.note: Thai green curry paste is built on shrimp paste and finished with fish sauce, so not vegan. Wheat is not inherent but is not ruled out. Ask.

items.ja: マッサマンカレー（ハーブと野菜のピーナッツ入りココナッツミルクカレー・鶏肉）
items.en: Massaman curry with peanuts, herbs and vegetables, chicken
items.note: Massaman paste contains shrimp paste as standard; contains peanuts, which the shop names.

items.ja: シューシークン（揚げ海老のココナッツカレーソース）
items.en: Fried prawns in coconut curry sauce, ☆
items.note: The prawns are battered and fried before saucing.

items.ja: ゲーンパネーン(レッドココナッツカレー) 鶏肉／豚肉
items.en: Panang red coconut curry, chicken or pork, ☆
items.note: Shrimp-paste-based curry paste and fish sauce.

items.ja: グリーンカレーうどん
items.note: ⚠ UDON IS WHEAT, and this is the only wheat noodle filed under CURRIES rather than under 麺 — easy to miss if you are scanning the noodle block for what to avoid.

items.ja: カオラーガパオ(バジル炒めごはん) 豚肉／鶏肉
items.en: Holy-basil stir-fry over rice, pork or chicken, ☆☆
items.note: Rice is clean; the gapao seasoning carries oyster and fish sauce. Usually topped with a fried egg.

items.ja: カオオッサッパロッス(パイナップルチャーハン)
items.note: Thai fried rice is seasoned with soy or fish sauce and normally carries egg and dried shrimp or floss.

items.ja: カオマンガイ(タイ風チキンライス)
items.note: The rice is cooked in chicken stock and the defining dipping sauce is a fermented soybean paste (taochiao) with soy sauce — wheat by default.

items.ja: カオパットムヤムクン／カオパッキョウワン／カオパックン／カオパッムー
items.romaji: khao pad tom yum kung / keow wan / kung / moo
items.en: Fried rice — tom yum, green curry, prawn or pork
items.note: Fried rice here is seasoned with soy or fish sauce and contains egg.

items.ja: カオクルックカピ(タイのビビンバ海老みそ混ぜご飯)
items.en: Rice mixed with shrimp paste, Thai-style
items.note: Kapi is shrimp paste — emphatically not vegan; wheat status of the paste unpublished.

items.ja: カオホウムマリ(ジャスミンライス)
items.note: Plain steamed jasmine rice — one ingredient, no wheat and no animal product. On a card this heavily sauced it is the reliable base.

items.ja: カオニャオ(餅米)
items.note: Steamed glutinous rice. The name 'glutinous' refers to its texture, not to gluten — it is rice and contains no wheat.

items.ja: パッタイクン(タイ風焼きそば)
items.note: The noodle is RICE. The pad thai sauce is tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce — and Japanese-market pad thai sauces frequently add soy. Contains egg, dried shrimp and peanuts. Ask about the sauce, not the noodle.

items.ja: トムヤムクンヌードル(トムヤムクン米粉麺)
items.en: Tom yum kung with RICE-FLOUR noodles, ☆☆
items.note: The shop states 米粉 — rice flour — on the card itself, which is the clearest noodle statement it makes anywhere. The broth's chilli paste and fish sauce remain the open question.

items.ja: カオソーイ(ココナッツカレーヌードル)
items.en: Khao soi — northern Thai coconut curry noodles, ☆
items.note: ⚠ THE TRAP IN THIS SECTION. Khao soi is made with WHEAT EGG NOODLES, both boiled and fried as a crisp topping — it is the one dish in a rice-noodle block that is not rice. Nothing on the card says so.

items.ja: クイッティオ ガイ／ムウ／ヌァトゥン
items.romaji: kuay teow gai / moo / nuea tun
items.en: Clear rice-noodle soup — chicken, pork or braised beef
items.note: クイッティオ is a rice noodle. The stock is a meat broth and the braised-beef version is simmered in soy sauce and five spice, so that one is wheat by default.

items.ja: パッシーユー(太麺焼きそば)
items.note: ⚠ The dish is NAMED for its sauce: see ew means SOY SAUCE. The wide noodle is rice, but the seasoning that defines the dish is soy, so it is wheat by default.

items.ja: パッキーマオタレー(海鮮激辛太麺焼きそば)
items.note: Same wide rice noodle, same soy-and-oyster seasoning family as pad see ew.

items.ja: スキヘン(汁なし春雨麺)／スキナム(汁あり春雨麺)
items.en: Thai suki with glass noodles, dry or in broth, ☆☆
items.note: The glass noodle is mung-bean starch, but suki sauce is built on fermented BEAN CURD and soy sauce, which is the wheat in this dish.

items.ja: クルイトードアイティム(揚げバナナ春巻きのココナッツアイス添え)
items.en: Fried banana spring roll with coconut ice cream
items.note: Wheat spring-roll wrapper, fried.

items.ja: カノムモーケン(焼きプリン)／モーケンアイティム
items.en: Thai baked custard, alone or with coconut ice cream
items.note: Mor kaeng is coconut milk, palm sugar and EGG, often with mung bean; some recipes add wheat flour. Ask.

items.ja: マンモプニン(マンゴープリン)／マンゴープリンセット
items.en: Mango pudding, alone or set with sticky rice and coconut ice cream
items.note: Japanese mango pudding is normally set with gelatine and contains dairy. Ask.

items.ja: カノムトゥアイ(ココナッツプリン)
items.en: Steamed coconut pudding in a cup
items.note: Traditional kanom tuay is coconut milk, rice flour and palm sugar — plant and wheat-free in its classic form, which makes it the most promising dessert here. The shop publishes no recipe, so ask.

items.ja: サクー(タピオカココナッツミルク)／アイスクリームガティー&サクー
items.en: Tapioca in coconut milk, alone or with coconut ice cream
items.note: Tapioca is cassava starch and coconut milk is plant — a plausible vegan dessert. Whether the coconut ice cream contains dairy is not stated. Ask.

items.ja: ブァロイ(タイ風おしるこ)
items.en: Thai rice-flour dumplings in coconut milk
items.note: Bua loy dumplings are glutinous RICE flour in coconut milk — no wheat in the classic recipe, though a poached egg is added in some versions. Ask.

items.ja: アイスクリームガティー(ココナッツアイスクリーム)
items.note: Traditional kati ice cream is coconut milk only, but many Japanese-supplied versions add dairy. Ask.

tokyo_kaisen_izakaya_uohide_sh.price_note: Prices 税込, from the shop's own HotPepper page (渋谷区宇田川町35-6 下田ビルB1F — the record's Udagawa-cho placement). ⚠ THE SHOP RUNS TWO KITCHENS ON ONE CARD and that is the useful thing to know here: a Japanese seafood izakaya section and a whole 「魚秀のヨコ飯（洋食）」 Western section with pizza, pasta, gratin, napolitan and baguette. So the wheat is not confined to the tempura corner — it is spread across an entire second half of the menu that a traveller scanning for 'fish izakaya' would not expect. ⚠ Everything in 【揚げたて】 is battered or crumbed: the 天ぷら盛り and 野菜天ぷら盛り are tempura batter, the すり身天ぷら and ちくわチーズいそべ揚げ are fish-paste fritters, あじフライ and カキフライ and カニクリームコロッケ are panko. ⚠ The shop's headline is its 飲める海鮮ユッケ range — raw seafood in a house 特製ダレ, and yukhoe dressing is soy sauce and sesame oil, so the entire signature section is wheat by default. Same for the sushi, the maki, the ochazuke and both miso soups. ⚠ VEGAN: essentially nothing. 冷やしトマトガリ添え, きゅうり浅漬け and アボカドスライス are the plant items; the 冷奴 comes with sudachi, and 熱々アンチョビキャベツ is anchovy despite reading as a cabbage dish.

items.note: Nikomi is simmered in miso and soy.

tokyo_arabiki_soba_toki.price_note: ⚠ READ THIS ONE IF YOU AVOID GLUTEN, BECAUSE IT IS THE RAREST CLAIM IN THE WHOLE TOKYO SET AND IT STILL DOES NOT MEAN WHAT YOU WANT IT TO MEAN. The house standing rule for this dataset is that even 十割 (100% buckwheat) soba means 打ち粉 — the wheat flour dusted on the board and the cut noodles to stop them sticking — and a shared boiling pot. This shop is the exception that states otherwise IN WRITING. Its menu card, transcribed by a diner at moritatoa.com, reads 「つなぎ粉も打ち粉も一切使わない純粋な国産十割蕎麦です」— no binding flour AND no dusting flour, at all, pure domestic 100% buckwheat — followed by 「野趣あふれる粗挽き蕎麦はざくざく噛み締めて召し上がって」. The operator’s own site says the same thing about the flour: 山形産の超粗挽き蕎麦粉のみを使用した…十割蕎麦, and 蕎麦は全て粗挽き国産粉十割 — ALL the soba, not one line of it. Retty adds that the flour is specially stone-milled and, outside Toki, goes only to one Osaka ryōtei. ⚠ AND NOW THE PART THAT KEEPS IT AT “ask”: the noodle is not the meal. The つゆ is dashi and soy sauce, and soy sauce is wheat. The kitchen deep-fries かしわ天 — chicken in tempura batter — in oil that is not claimed to be dedicated. The shop publishes no allergen policy and makes no gluten-free claim; what it makes is a purity claim about its flour, for texture reasons, and those are not the same thing. What it does give a coeliac is something almost no soba shop in Tokyo does: a plausible route to eating the actual noodle, if you can get it served with salt, wasabi and grated daikon instead of tsuyu, or bring your own tamari. Ask. ⚠ PRICES ARE OLD AND MIXED. The itemised figures come from a Retty editorial piece dated 2018/03/08 and are marked 税別 — pre-tax-exclusive, and from before the October 2019 rise to 10%. The two 税込 figures come from an undated blog whose author mentions eating out being restricted, placing it in the 2020–21 period. The operator’s own site publishes no prices at all and Gnavi lists dish names with none. Instagram is the record’s listed website and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ BETTER URL FOUND: this record was filed as social-only, but the shop has a first-party page under its operator, Itteki Group, at https://www.itteki.com/toki.html — 東京都渋谷区代々木2-14-3, 03-6304-2566.

items.ja: もりそば
items.en: Mori soba — the cold noodles alone on a slatted tray with dipping tsuyu on the side. At this shop that means coarse-milled Yamagata buckwheat, 100% and nothing else, cut thick enough that the menu tells you to chew it
items.note: ⚠ THE NOODLE MAY BE THE CLEANEST SOBA NOODLE IN TOKYO AND THE SAUCE IS STILL WHEAT. 店の品書き：つなぎ粉も打ち粉も一切使わない純粋な国産十割蕎麦。No binding wheat and — unusually, and stated by the shop itself — no dusting wheat either, so the noodle and the water it boils in should both be buckwheat only. The つゆ it is dipped in is bonito dashi and soy sauce: wheat, and fish. Order it and then negotiate the sauce; salt, wasabi and grated daikon are the traditional alternative and this is a shop that would understand the request. Buckwheat itself is a declared allergen in Japan for the opposite reason — if soba is what you react to, none of this shop is available to you at all.

items.ja: おつまみかしわ天
items.en: Chicken tempura as a drinking snack — kashiwa is the Kansai and Kyushu word for chicken, which tells you something about the kitchen’s lineage
items.note: 天ぷら＝小麦の衣。Tempura batter is wheat flour, straight. Chicken. This is also the item that puts a wheat fryer in a shop whose noodles are wheat-free — worth knowing before treating the soba as safe.

items.ja: かしわ天（ランチ・3個）
items.en: Chicken tempura added to a lunch, three pieces
items.note: Same wheat batter, sold as a lunchtime add-on at a third of the evening price.

items.ja: お得セット
items.en: The value set — soba plus chicken tempura plus a bowl of tororo rice. The lunch most people order
items.note: The set is built around the two things that undo the noodle: wheat-battered chicken tempura, and a tsuyu-based tororo rice. とろろめしは出汁と醤油で調味されるのが一般的。If you are here for the buckwheat, order the soba alone and skip the set.

items.ja: しじみ出汁おでん（5種盛り）
items.en: Oden simmered in freshwater-clam broth, five pieces — the clams are from Jūsan-ko in Aomori, which is the lake Japan associates with shijimi
items.note: しじみ＝貝、おでんだしは醤油ベース。The broth is shellfish, so this is a mollusc dish before it is anything else. Oden broth is soy-seasoned, and the standard oden pot contains 竹輪・はんぺん・さつま揚げ, all of which are fish paste bound with wheat starch. Which five pieces is not published.

items.ja: 冷やし鶏そば
items.en: Chilled chicken soba — pictured on both the operator’s site and Gnavi as a signature, with no price published on either
items.note: Same 100% buckwheat noodle; chicken, and a chilled broth that will be dashi-and-soy based. Chicken makes it not vegetarian; the broth makes it wheat.

items.ja: 辛味大根しぼりそば
items.en: Soba with the pressed juice of hot daikon — the Shinshu way of eating soba, where the sharp radish liquid replaces or cuts the sauce
items.note: WORTH ASKING ABOUT SPECIFICALLY. 辛味大根のしぼり汁は本来つゆの代わり、ただし多くの店はつゆを合わせる。In its original form this dish is buckwheat noodles, pressed radish juice and salt — no soy sauce and no dashi, which would make it the one bowl in the shop that is both wheat-free and plant-only. Most Tokyo shops mix the juice into ordinary tsuyu instead, which puts back both the wheat and the fish. This shop publishes neither the price nor the method. If any single question is worth asking at this counter, it is this one.

items.ja: 純米酒（週替わり約20種）
items.en: Junmai sake, around twenty labels from across Japan, changed weekly and chosen by the owner. The shop bills itself as a soba-and-junmai bar rather than a noodle shop, and is built for drinking alone
items.note: 純米酒は米・米麹・水のみ（法令上の定義）。The one drink in this shop a coeliac can order without a conversation: junmai is defined in law as rice, rice koji and water and nothing else — no brewer’s alcohol, no additives, no barley. That is a real distinction from beer, whisky-highballs and barley shochu, all of which are barley. Plant-based.

items.ja: 壱岐麦焼酎 ちんぐ
items.en: Chingu — a barley shochu from Iki, the island off Kyushu that is one of Japan’s protected shochu origins and the place barley shochu is said to have started
items.note: 麦焼酎＝大麦が原料。麦は日本の表示義務対象外。Barley is the raw material, and barley is NOT on Japan’s statutory allergen list, so nothing on the bottle has to tell you. Distillation leaves essentially no gluten protein behind and most coeliac guidance treats distilled spirits as safe — but if you avoid barley on principle rather than by protein, this is barley. The junmai sake beside it is not.
